newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Liebenberg praises Manuel and his S.African budget.
newsitem.headline: Liebenberg praises Manuel and his S.African budget.

text.p: South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel's maiden budget presented on Wednesday afternoon was praised by his predecessor, banker Chris Liebenberg.

"I think that the budget showed that it was time for a politician to take over the finance portfolio. I think he was bold and I think that his delivery was outstanding," Liebenberg told reporters after Manuel delivered his 1997/98 budget speech in parliament.
Manuel had a rough reception in the markets last year after he was appointed as replacement for Liebenberg, who announced his retirement from office shortly after presenting the 1996/97 budget.
On the lifting of exchange controls, he said that Manuel had "gone as far as he possibly could under current circumstances and I admire him for what he has done".
On whether Manuel would be able to meet his budget deficit targets, Liebenberg said: "Definitely. He has proved up to now that he has delivered what he has promised.

"I think that one of the things that this government has done very effectively, that people don't realise, is that (for) every budget that they have laid on the table they have delivered on all the deficits.
"And again Trevor Manuel has done it today. I think it is to be admired," Liebenberg said.
